old_caption:
The video captures a close-up view inside an air fryer, showcasing a batch of food items being cooked. The air fryer's glass door is closed, allowing a clear view of the contents inside. The food appears to be small, square-shaped pieces, possibly breaded or coated in some manner, arranged neatly on the air fryer's tray. The pieces vary slightly in color, suggesting different stages of cooking or varying ingredients used.

In the background, through the reflective surface of the air fryer, a kitchen setting is visible. A dining table with chairs can be seen, along with various items placed on it, such as a bottle and some papers. The reflection also shows part of the kitchen counter and cabinets, indicating a well-lit environment. The camera remains stationary throughout the video, focusing solely on the air fryer's interior and the cooking process. There are no noticeable changes in the position or appearance of the food items during the sequence, implying that the video is capturing a moment

caption: The video captures a glass-fronted appliance with a metallic lower frame, viewed straight on from the front. Inside, on a dark reflective tray, dozens of small upright cubes are laid out in a loose triangular cluster, with gaps between many of them. Most cubes are pale cream or white, with a few brown ones near the center, and one isolated cube sits apart at the far left. Through and around the glass a kitchen is visible, with a dark table and chairs on the left, light cabinets and a hanging towel on the right, and a striped reflection plus a dark shape at the top center. The cubes and their arrangement appear unchanged, with no visible movement of the isolated left cube, the central brown cubes, or the cubes toward the right edge. The background and the glass reflections also appear stable, with no obvious pan, tilt, or zoom.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Inside, on a dark reflective tray, dozens of small cubes are laid out in a loose triangular cluster that points toward the viewer. Most cubes are pale cream or white, with a few brown ones near the center, and one isolated cube sits apart at the far left. Through and around the glass a kitchen is visible, with a dark table and chairs on the left, light cabinets and a hanging towel on the right, and a striped reflection plus a dark shape at the top center.
